items.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010
items.q: My first band was Woody Herman and that was like my first professional jazz gig so to speak.

ctx.x: You had your big band experiences under three kind of different leaders. You had Mel Lewis and Buddy Rich and Woody Herman. Who did you enjoy the most?

Well I can’t, that’s a hard — here I could explain it in a certain way. My first band was Woody Herman and that was like my first professional jazz gig so to speak. I mean I’d played a lot of gigs, but I don’t mean professional as far as getting paid, but upper eschelons jazz. And Woody, and I just learned a lot. I learned a lot from Woody because of the fact that I finally realized that a leader has to trust you. I don’t mean just showing up on time, but the music and showing up on time, and just being there for…
To trust you to not only play but —
